findings.evidence: The item calls the displayed functions probability densities and asserts E|z|^2=1, but its dependencies do not establish the real density normalization, real second moment, transformed complex density, or variance-one moment. The available lem-normal-density-has-total-mass-one assumes full AC, not just Countable Choice, and is not a dependency. Downstream Gaussian invariance, rank, pseudoinverse-moment, and expectation proofs rely on these probability-law facts. A Countable-Choice-compatible normalization and moment result, including finite product normalization, is needed.

The Definition asserts that the finite-scan basis and projector are Borel functions, but algorithmic properties must be established in a separate proved result. Expected-error consumers need this measurability to define their expectations. A separate result with the finite-stratum proof is needed; none is assigned in this batch.

The Definition asserts measurability of each selected basis/projector as a procedure property, without a separate proved result. The power-transfer and expected-error consumers need a measurable projector. A separate result proving measurability of the repeated finite-scan composition is needed; none is assigned in this batch.

The summary says the examples show exact rank-k recovery almost surely. The assigned exact-recovery example relies on the wide-Gaussian full-row-rank almost-sure claim, which uses the Gaussian law as a probability measure; the assigned law definition lacks a Countable-Choice-compatible normalization and variance-one justification. B-page prose was outside this assignment's edit scope.
